scope: Independent review of DKM paper mapping, Bernoulli risk calibration, KT adaptation and conservative numerical certificates. This is not official-code replication or a performance-superiority verdict.

algorithm_mapping.implementation: Paid one-pull-per-arm initialization; initial tracking target equals these paid counts.
Bernoulli KL intervals with f(t)=x+log(x)+1/2, x=(1+a)(1+b)log(t); weighted model projection inside the interval box; answer is the sign of its C.
Current-count projection and selected sign are now tested against the same current counts before the next paid draw. A terminal unused allocation computation is recorded explicitly.
A separate AdaHedge instance for each answer selects arm weights; the lambda player uses a numerical opposite-answer KL best response.
Optimistic payoffs maximize endpoint KL and f(t)/N; negative payoffs update the selected answer learner.
Cumulative RATIO tracking argmin N/sum(w), matching the printed algorithm.

kk21_review.formula: sum_a 3 log(1+log N_a) + K C_exp(log(1/delta)/K), with C_exp from Theorem 7 equations (9)-(10), equivalently Proposition 15 equation (20).
kk21_review.family: The generic exponential-family/Bernoulli result is used; no Gaussian-only calibration is substituted.
kk21_review.global_control: On any incorrect selected sign, the true physical parameter belongs to that opposite closed cone. The saturated/null GLR is no larger than sum_a N_a KL(empirical_a,true_a); Theorem 7/Proposition 15 control the same all-arm event for either selected direction, including C=0.
kk21_review.boundary: For p=0 or 1, apply the interior Bernoulli result to a physical contraction toward A=1/2, use continuity of finite-history event probabilities, then increase the finite time horizon. This extends risk validity, not the exact-oracle efficiency theorem.
kk21_review.arithmetic: Machin/Basel constant bounds, monotone h-inverse upper bracketing, monotone h-tilde evaluation and outward likelihood tangents produce conservative threshold/likelihood bounds. Independent 100-digit comparisons cover 20 calibration and 20 count-dependent threshold cases.

kt_safe_review.name: A separately named DKM-sampling plus product-Jeffreys universal-inference adaptation.
kt_safe_review.proof: The product of fixed per-arm Jeffreys marginal likelihoods is one normalized Q under predictable arm choices. Every erroneous sign threshold crossing Q/sup_opposite L implies Q/L_true >=1/delta; both signs share this same likelihood-ratio event. A factor-two directional threshold is unnecessary.
kt_safe_review.boundary: On support edges Q/L_true is a nonnegative supermartingale on the realized support; the common-event argument still applies.

official_code_boundary.tracking_difference: Cached tidnabbil_tracking.jl CTracking uses argmin(N-sumw), whereas the printed DKM algorithm and this implementation use argmin(N/sumw).
official_code_boundary.threshold_difference: Cached tidnabbil_thresholds.jl uses the GK16 empirical log((log(t)+1)/delta) threshold. The implemented KK21 bound is a conservative proven Bernoulli choice, not a recreation of the paper plot threshold.

corrected_issues: The initial driver tested fresh counts with a stale pre-pull label; the frozen driver now selects and tests on the same current counts before drawing.

Initial SLSQP success flags admitted poor best responses. The frozen objective has a matching convex linear extension, nondegenerate cone constraints, pooled restarts, feasible line corrections and a convex-gap gate. The initial issue artifact is preserved separately.

validation.implementation_checks_reviewed: 16 independent 100-digit threshold comparisons, 49-round high-precision AdaHedge comparison, per-step confidence/optimism/tracking/RNG reconstruction, current-label verification and engineering probes including a 4096-shot null path.

limitations: The default six registered rational arms differ from FaultTune continuous rational-angle selection; comparisons must name the grid or add a matched-grid control.

Design uses a 1e-6 interior physical margin and numerical SLSQP oracles. The stopping certificate uses the entire closed physical null, so the design restriction affects efficiency rather than risk validity.

The best-response 1e-5 gap gate is an absolute floating diagnostic, not a certified relative-error guarantee. It can be material on very weak-signal games; log it and do not inherit exact-oracle sample-complexity claims.

Projection failure may retain a previous answer. Exact DKM permits arbitrary answers for an empty model/confidence intersection, while numerical failure is an additional implementation limitation; report projection failures.
batch_size>1 is an explicitly named allocation adaptation. check_every>1 also coarsens the stopping schedule. Neither reproduces the original per-observation stopping trajectory.
C=0 is protected against either directional claim and may remain undecided at the finite cap; no finite stopping guarantee at zero is asserted.
Official Julia code was located and read in part, but it has not been run or matched step by step. No full-field SOTA or mathematical novelty claim follows.
